subject: Managed identities & IP lockdown runbook for onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sethi <cloudops@brightlinehealth.com>, security@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: managed identities & IP allowlist questions

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re moving fast on the onboarding timeline and I wanted to surface a couple of items the security and cloud teams asked us to confirm before we schedule a staging cutover:

1) SSO / SAML: we’ll be responsible for IdP metadata and Okta config. Can you send a checklist for required attributes, cert rotation cadence, and recommended assertion lifetime?

2) SCIM: we have a fairly strict schema (custom title and dept fields). Do you have a sample SCIM mapping and supported attribute types?

3) IP allowlist: our infra team wants to know the CIDR blocks you provision for Hosted vs Dedicated. We may need edge IP ranges retained for firewall rules.

4) Service accounts: we need patterns for ephemeral service identities vs long-lived service accounts for automated provisioning. Any policy recommendations?

Also attaching the SSO onboarding questionnaire we were given. Can you share a runbook or operational playbook your team follows so we can align next week?

Thanks,
Alex Monroe
Technical Program Manager, Brightline Health
Alex.Monroe@brightlinehealth.com

Attachments:
- brightline_onboarding_questionnaire.pdf (attachment)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: managed identities & IP allowlist questions

Alex —

Great questions and thanks for sending the questionnaire. I’ve sketched a pragmatic runbook below to cover SSO/SAML, SCIM, IP allowlisting, and service account patterns. I’m sharing three quick artifacts with this email: 1) ip-allowlist-template.csv, 2) scim-schema-v2.yml, 3) a one-page mutual action plan PDF.

High-level runbook (staging cutover path):
- Week 0: Security alignment call (SAML certs, assertion ttl, required attributes).
- Week 1: SCIM mapping + test users (we recommend a small test group of 5 accounts to validate attribute sync).
- Week 2: IP allowlist dry-run (add Hosted CIDRs to staging firewall; Dedicated will have fixed egress ranges).
- Week 3: Service account provisioning and least-privilege checks (ephemeral tokens for deployment hooks, long-lived for audit services).
- Week 4: Cutover weekend (fallback rollback plan included in the PDF).

Key notes:
- SAML: Redwood accepts standard NameID formats; we recommend 1 hour assertion TTL for interactive flows and 15m for programmatic assertion exchange. We support multiple certs for rotation; we’ll provide metadata endpoint for automatic fetch.
- SCIM: Our SCIM supports custom attributes (string, boolean, array); see attached scim-schema-v2.yml. If you have custom title/dept we’ll map those to enterprise:jobTitle and enterprise:department.
- IP allowlist: see ip-allowlist-template.csv. Hosted CIDRs are dynamic but we can provide a daily JSON feed and a set of static NAT ranges for Dedicated customers.
- Service accounts: recommended pattern is ephemeral tokens for CI/CD with a short TTL + a managed service account for backup/audit tasks (rotate quarterly).

Immediate asks from us to you:
1) Confirm a three-hour window during Week 3 for the staging allowlist dry-run.
2) Share a sample Okta metadata object (or IdP endpoint) and two test users for SCIM.
3) Point of contact for firewall ops (I’ll loop Jordan for the NAT ranges).

I’ll have Monica and Ben pick up the detailed task list and assign owners — Monica will lead SCIM mapping and Ben will own network coordination.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachments:
- ip-allowlist-template.csv (attachment)
- scim-schema-v2.yml (attachment)
- brightline-mutual-action-plan.pdf (attachment)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Marcus / Ben —

Looping here with an operational breakdown. Quoting Marcus: 

> - Week 1: SCIM mapping + test users (we recommend a small test group of 5 accounts to validate attribute sync).

Action plan (SCIM & attributes) — Monica owns delivery:
- Day 0 (receipt): I will validate Brightline's SCIM connector can read enterprise:jobTitle and enterprise:department.
- Day 1: I’ll import two test users you provide and run attribute diffs; I’ll capture failures to scim-sync.log.
- Day 2: Create and share a short runbook with Okta mapping screenshots.
- Day 3: Hand back to Alex for acceptance testing; I’ll be available real-time for sync troubleshooting.

Network / IP allowlist tasks (Ben):
- Ben to provide static Dedicated egress set and the daily Hosted JSON feed endpoint.
- Coordinate with Priya on firewall acceptance window; propose staging window: 2027-05-29 02:00–05:00 UTC.

Service account policy notes:
- Ephemeral tokens: integrate Redwood short-lived credential endpoint in CI/CD (rotate per deploy).
- Long-lived: create minimal-scope service identity for audit exports (rotate on quarterly schedule).

Deliverables I’ll produce: SCIM runbook (doc link), sync test logs, and a final mapping spreadsheet.

Monica Patel
Senior Implementation Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
